what: Everything the person sells, as photo tiles in shelves by state (spec/pages.md §6.10), filtered by one row.

frame.who: Clearing out (primary, 11 things on 3 sites) checks it a few times a day; the flipper (64 things) lives in it; a new person sees it empty once.
frame.came_to: See where each thing is (needs me, live, sold) at a glance and open the one they mean; the flipper also narrows by site and sorts.
frame.mistake_costs_most: A bulk change that ends listings or deletes items: it is public and slow to undo, so it hands off with exactly what it will do written on the button.
frame.ways_out: Select many and change them at once (Keep, Donated, Sold elsewhere, Delete; ways-out §6.10 and §6.6); Pause selling from the foot of the page (ways-out, Everywhere); the empty page leads straight to the camera.
frame.in_the_loop: The agent never acts from this page; the tile shows where it is (Researching, Needs you), and a bulk change waits for one tap on a button that says what it does.

decisions.decision: Two columns of square tiles, everywhere
decisions.why: The round 11 Sell Ben reacted to was two columns; at two the title and the money line fit, and the tag and site logos sit on a photo big enough to read them (Depop and Instagram grids, copy.md). Pinch density in sell/grid.ts is left for the phone build.

decisions.decision: One row of filters: sort, then each site as its logo; once one shelf is open alone (See all), All and each shelf with its count join it
decisions.why: Ben, round 11: "you only needed one horizontal y value for the filtering". On the whole page the shelves already name themselves with their counts, so a chip per shelf said each one twice (U19, Ben 10:27: "a lot of clutter"); alone, a shelf has no header and the chips are the way back and across.

decisions.decision: Sort is the first chip and says its pick ("Latest", "Price, high")
decisions.why: A sort hidden in an icon has to be remembered; a chip that names it shows the order the grid is in, as Vinted and Depop filter rows do.

decisions.decision: The state tag on the photo's top left, the site badges on its bottom right corner, 4 apart
decisions.why: Ben, round 11: "where the icon is on the image", as the dark Today draws it (Art. 7.8). Badges never overlap, so every logo shows whole (C5).

decisions.decision: Shelves are sections of the grid, two rows each, with See all; no sideways shelves
decisions.why: pages §6.10 says each shelf scrolls sideways, but a sideways shelf under a sideways filter row is two horizontal gestures stacked, and the decided Sell is a photo grid. Two rows and See all keep the flipper's 64 things to one screen a shelf.

decisions.decision: Every shelf folds and opens from its header; Unsold and Kept start folded
decisions.why: Ben, 06:19: "I wish on the sell site like the needs you and in progress parts they were collapsible" (product/words.md#2026-11-15-notes-on-the-first-gallery-today-must-explain-itself-you-is-a-dashboard-the-camera-frames-the-listing-photo). Unsold and Kept are not for sale, so they start folded (pages §6.10).

decisions.decision: Needs you is in Today's order, not newest first
decisions.why: An offer that runs out tonight must not sit behind 40 fresh drafts (pages §5: what ignoring it costs, then the deadline). Any sort the person picks wins.

decisions.decision: On Needs you, a tile whose pill only says where it is shows what is asked ("Question", "Scam", "Price")
decisions.why: A Live tag under the "Needs you" heading contradicts it; the decision kind is what the person has to do.

decisions.decision: The second line is one fact: Listed at, Offered, You get, Worth (a range in whole dollars), Pricing
decisions.why: pages §3, what each persona looks at first: clearing wants "is it gone yet" and the money; the line never repeats the tag.

decisions.decision: Sold things show the money's word: On its way, Ready on the site, In your bank (the tag turns Paid)
decisions.why: spec/edge-cases.md §2 (Ben and a mentor, 05:05). The dates and instant payout with its fee sit on the order, on the item page, never as a default.

decisions.decision: Select is a gray pill in the title row, beside the inbox (TabNav action); Done takes its place while picking. The change is picked in a sheet and waits for a button that says exactly what it does
decisions.why: ways-out §6.10 "200 items: select many, then one change for all"; iOS Photos puts Select in its title row, and a row of its own under the title was one more line before the first tile (U11, Art. 7.12). Ending listings is public, so it hands off with its count of listings on the button (ui-build hand-off rule).

decisions.decision: Keep, Donated and Sold elsewhere act with Undo; Delete has none and skips anything with an open order, saying so in the row
decisions.why: ways-out §6.6: Keep or Donated sets kept with its reason; Sold elsewhere closes it; Delete is refused while an order is open and cannot be undone.

decisions.decision: Pause selling is a plain ruled row at the foot
decisions.why: Art. 7.9: what a person can do to the page's subject that is not today's decision sits in ruled rows at the end; ways-out "I'm away for two weeks" lives in You > Pause selling.

decisions.decision: Empty: one line, "Nothing for sale", and Sell something, which opens the camera
decisions.why: copy.md C11 and pages §6.10 ("the ＋ is the only thing to point to"); one display heading per view, so the page title gives way to it.

decisions.decision: Loading is four gray tiles under the title, with no filters, counts or Select
decisions.why: Art. 5, Loading: the skeleton mirrors the grid so nothing moves; a count shown before the things arrive would be a guess.

decisions.decision: Failed says the things didn’t load, with Try again; offline keeps the last copy and a change waits, its button saying Waiting for signal
decisions.why: ways-out, Everywhere: nothing is guessed, and a tap without signal is held, not lost (as Today holds it).

decisions.decision: The header is the press: title, count and a chevron that turns right when folded and down when open; See all stays on the right
decisions.why: The way a section folds in Files and Reminders. The count shows in both states so a folded shelf still says how much is in it; the header is one size in both, so folding moves nothing in it (U7).

decisions.decision: The fold opens with a fade and the shelves below glide, in the select time (shelfFold, 200 ms, ease-out)
decisions.why: frontend-standard §3: a state change, done tens of times a day, so short and subtle; opacity and transform only; under Reduce Motion it is instant.

decisions.decision: Each fold is remembered for the person
decisions.why: Someone who folds Live every visit should not have to fold it again. Kept in memory for the demo and in the browser on the web.

decisions.decision: Sell carries the wash
decisions.why: Ben, 06:21: "sometimes the gradient at the top of the screen is there or isnt there" (product/words.md#2026-11-15-notes-on-the-first-gallery-today-must-explain-itself-you-is-a-dashboard-the-camera-frames-the-listing-photo). The wash sits on every main tab and on no pushed page or sheet.

decisions.decision: A tile is titled with the thing's short name, not the listing title
decisions.why: Art. 7.15: a title is read whole; the photo already says which thing, and the listing's details are on the item page. Photos and eBay's selling grid show a name, never a description.
